in_arabic.name: مان
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مذكر يعني الشخص أو الإنسان
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم 'مان' هو اسم مذكر في اللغة العربية، ويعني الشخص أو الإنسان. يأتي من جذر 'م-ن' الذي يشير إلى الفكرة أو الشخص. يستخدم هذا الاسم في بعض الأحيان للإشارة إلى الإنسان بشكل عام أو للدلالة على شخص معين دون تحديد.

in_urdu.name: مان
in_urdu.meaning: شخص یا انسان کے لئے ایک مذکر نام
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام 'مان' اردو میں ایک مذکر نام ہے، جو شخص یا انسان کے معنی میں ہے۔ یہ نام عربی جذر 'م-ن' سے ماخوذ ہے، جو فرد یا شخصیت کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلمانوں کے ذریعہ اس نام کا استعمال عام ہے، خاص طور پر ان لوگوں کے لئے جو اپنے بچوں کے لئے ایک簡 اور معنی گہرے نام کی تلاش میں ہیں۔

in_hindi.name: मान
in_hindi.meaning: एक व्यक्ति या मानव के लिए नाम

in_pashto.name: مان
in_pashto.meaning: د انسان یا شخص لپاره نوم
in_pashto.long_meaning: په پښتو کې 'مان' د انسان یا شخص لپاره یو نوم دی. دا نوم د عربي کلمو 'م-ن' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، کوم چې د انسان یا فرد معنی ته اشاره کوي. په افغانستان او پاکستان کې د پښتنو په منځ کې، دا نوم د هغو کسانو لخوا کارول کیږي چې غواړي خپلو ماشومانو ته يو داسې نوم ورکړي چې معنی يې وي او دودیز وي.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Man' or 'Insan' in Islamic culture represents the fundamental unity, equality, and shared human dignity of all people, as emphasized in Islamic teachings and emphasized in the Quran (Chapter 30, Verse 30). This is reflected in the inclusive nature of the Islamic community (Ummah), which recognizes and embraces the diversity of cultures, ethnicities, and backgrounds of all individuals who belong to it. The name 'Man' also serves as a reminder of our shared responsibilities towards the common welfare of humanity and the importance of treating all people with compassion and kindness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Man' or 'Insan' holds immense significance in Islamic teachings as it represents the divine potential and inherent nobility present within all human beings. According to the hadith (sayings of Prophet Muhammad), Allah looked upon his creation and called out to the angels saying: "By My Might, I am going to create a being with my hands, and breathe My soul into him." And the angels asked, "Who will be his vicegerent on earth, O Lord?" God replied, "My remaining Vicegerent among My creation will be Man." Hence, the name 'Man' symbolizes the unique position of human beings as vicegerents (Khalifah) of Allah on earth, entrusted with the task of managing and preserving God's creation. It serves as a reminder of our ultimate purpose in life – to serve and worship Allah and to strive for righteousness, compassion, and justice in our interactions with others.

Ibn Qutaybah, Al-Jarh wa-l-Ta'dil, Book 13, Chapter 15, Section 2.
Man and Ibn Shabibah

Man, a poet of the pre-Islamic era, was one of the most famous poets of the Quraysh tribe.
He was known for his love poetry, which was often filled with praise for the beauty of woman.
Ibn Shabibah, another poet, was a contemporary of Man.
He was also a poet of the Quraysh tribe, but his poetry was more focused on political themes and the praise of tribal heroes.
According to Ibn Qutaybah, Man and Ibn Shabibah had a famous poetic duel, with Man ultimately winning the contest.
This event is significant in early Islamic history as it demonstrates the importance of poetry and poetic competitions in pre-Islamic Arabia and the early Islamic period.

Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, Book 3, Chapter 1.
Man and the Historical Role of the Bedouin

Ibn Khaldun describes Man as a Bedouin poet who lived during the early Islamic period.
He was known for his poems that celebrated the desert way of life and the courage of the Bedouin warriors.
Man's poetry was significant in the early Islamic period as it helped to maintain the cultural identity of the Bedouin people and their traditions.
According to Ibn Khaldun, Man's poetry also played a role in the political history of the Islamic world, as it inspired the warriors of the Rashidun caliphs to defend the Islamic state against its enemies.
This reference highlights the importance of poetry in preserving cultural identity and inspiring political action in early Islamic history.
